description: A snack made with rice flour and chickpea flour, and deep fried.

name: Nachos
description: Fried corn tortillas covered with melted cheddar cheese, pickled jalapeño peppers, and other toppings.

name: Pita chips
description: Pita Bread cut into wedges or chips, that are oiled, seasoned, and baked until crispy.

name: Popcorn
description: A snack based on a variety of corn kernel which expands and puffs up when heated.

name: Potato chips
description: A thin slice of potato (or a thin deposit of potato paste) that has been deep fried, baked, or air fried until crunchy.

name: Prawn/fish crackers
description: A deep-fried snack made from starch and prawn or fish.

name: Pretzel, hard
description: Made from dough that is commonly shaped into a knot and baked hard to withstand a long shelf life.

name: Sev mamra
description: A mixture of spicy dry ingredients such as puffed rice, savory noodles and peanuts.

name: Snack mix
description: Refers to multiple types of snack items sold in supermarkets such as Chex Mix (pictured).

name: Tortilla chips
description: Wedges of fried corn tortillas; originated in Mexico; first produced commercially in Los Angeles, California, United States

name: Animal cracker
description: A small cracker or cookie baked in the shape of an animal, usually an animal one might see at a zoo.

name: Bagel chips
description: Small rounds sliced from bagels which are bread rolls with a dense, chewy, doughy interior and crispy exterior.

name: Barquillos
description: A batter of flour, eggs and other ingredients is cooked in a mold, re-shaped over heat and crisped-up upon cooling.

name: Center-filled crackers
description: These are small cracker biscuits with a crunchy crust and a sweet, creamy interior.

name: Crackers
description: A flat, dry baked biscuit typically made with flour, possibly flavored with herbs and spices before baking.

name: Graham crackers
description: Invented in Bound Brook, New Jersey by Sylvester Graham.

name: Hardtack
description: Hardtack (sometimes known colloquially as military dog biscuit) is a type of dense biscuit or cracker issued as provision or ration in the absence of perishable food.

name: Kuih cincin
description: Made from wheat and rice flour, palm sugar, and maltose or honey.

name: Maltose crackers
description: A popular traditional food in Hong Kong, consisting of maltose syrup sandwiched between two saltine crackers.

name: Oyster cracker
description: Small, salted crackers, often served with oyster stew and clam chowder and have a flavor similar to saltine crackers.

name: Rice cracker
description: It is an East Asian cracker made from rice flour such as Senbei (Japan).

name: Rusk
description: A hard, dry biscuit or a twice-baked bread, sometimes used as a teether for babies.

name: Soda cracker
description: A thin, usually square, cracker, made from white flour, sometimes yeast (although many are yeast free), and baking soda, with most varieties lightly sprinkled with coarse salt.

name: Wafer
description: A crispy, often sweet, very thin, flat, light biscuit that originated from the ninth century of Western Europe.

name: Water biscuit
description: A type of savory cracker that are thin, hard and brittle, usually served with cheese or wine.

name: Biltong
description: Spiced and air-dried beef, a popular snack during rugby games

name: Çiğ köfte
description: Middle Eastern raw meatball dish

name: Corn dog
description: A hot dog skewered on a stick, dipped in corn batter and deep-fried.

name: Instant noodles
description: A type of food consisting of noodles sold in a precooked and dried block with flavoring powder and/or seasoning oil.

name: Pasta
description: Pictured is cavatappi with pesto.

name: Ramen
description: Wheat noodles served in a soy- or miso-flavored meat or fish broth with toppings such as protein, seaweed, and green onions.

name: Yakisoba
description: A stir-fried dish of soba noodles made from buckwheat flour, often found as a snack food during Japanese festivals.

name: Curry
description: A sauce dish seasoned with spices, mainly associated with South Asian cuisine.

name: Hummus
description: A Middle Eastern dip, spread, or savory dish made from cooked, mashed chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon juice, and garlic.

name: Instant soup
description: Packaged soup stock that can be readily reconstituted from dry or paste ingredients (e.g. miso) into soup by adding hot water.

name: Jam
description: Preparations of fruits whose main preserving agent is sugar and sometimes acid, often stored in glass jars and used as a condiment or spread.

name: Taro paste
description: Yam paste, or Orh Nee 潮式芋泥 is a classic Teochew dessert.

name: Tongsui
description: Tongsui 糖水, literarily translated as sweet soup, are made from a grounded ingredient, which can be nuts, seeds or beans.

name: Yogurt
description: Yogurt is a highly viscous liquid in its original form and at room temperature.
